definition: A rare visceral arteriovenous malformation characterized by abnormal connections between uterine arteries and veins. Vaginal bleeding is the most common clinical feature, may be very severe, and is refractory to conventional treatments. Variable clinical features may include abdominal pulsatile masses, frequent urination or urinary incontinence, dyspareunia, and hematuria. Some patients remain asymptomatic.

A rare visceral arteriovenous malformation of the pancreas characterized by abnormal blood flow from the arterial system directly into the venous system without passing through the capillaries. Patients may present with episodic gastrointestinal bleeding or hemoperitoneum, epigastric or abdominal pain, pancreatitis, portal hypertension, and pseudocysts. Some patients remain asymptomatic.

A rare visceral arteriovenous malformation characterized by abnormal communications between renal arteries and the venous system. Most cases are asymptomatic but patients may present with clinical symptoms including hematuria, nausea, lumbar and abdominal pain, hypertension, cardiomegaly and high output heart failure. This type of malformation is more commonly reported in females.

A rare visceral arteriovenous malformation characterized by direct arterial-to-venous connections within the liver. Patients may be asymptomatic or present with symptoms such as anemia, consumptive coagulopathy, portal hypertension, hepatomegaly and may develop complications including congestive heart failure, necrosis of the liver or hydrops fetalis.

A rare visceral arteriovenous malformation characterized by abnormal communication between splenic artery and the splenic vein at the level of the splenic hilum. These malformations may lead to the formation of splenic artery aneurysms that can rupture. Clinical features include abdominal pain, hematemesis, melena, diarrhea, and portal hypertension due to venous congestion. The spleen is typically enlarged with extensive areas of infarction and dilated vessels.

A rare visceral arteriovenous malformation characterized by dilated and tortuous feeding arteries and veins of the gallblader. Patients present with abdominal pain. Association with hepatocellular carcinoma in some patients have been reported.

A rare visceral arteriovenous malformation characterized by abnormal communication between veins and arteries of the ureter, urethra, or urinary bladder. Major clinical signs include hematuria and suprapubic pain. Additional clinical features may include acute urinary retention and increased urinary frequency.

definition: A rare subtype of pontocerebellar hypoplasia (PCH) characterized by an almost complete absence of motor and cognitive development, microcephaly, epilepsy, spastic tetraplegia, vision impairment, extrapyramidal movements, and stereotypies. Brain imaging is distinct from other PCH subtypes and consists of mild-to-severe PCH, ventriculomegaly, thin corpus callosum and hypoplasia and T2-weighted hyperintensity of the basal ganglia and thalamus.

A rare subtype of pontocerebellar hypoplasia characterized by global developmental delay, motor impairment, axial hypotonia and distal hypotonia as well as severe brainstem dysfunctions (feeding and respiratory difficulties, central apnea, bradycardia). Other variable clinical features can include ophtalmological, cardiac and gastrointestinal anomalies, facial dysmorphism and epilepsy. This subtype is associated with perinatal lethality. Brain imaging usually shows cerebellar hypoplasia together with brainstem hypoplasia.
